# Performance overview

multiomeR is built on [`targets`](https://books.ropensci.org/targets/), which represents the workflow as a dependency graph. This makes the pipeline naturally parallelizable: whenever two targets do not depend on each other, `targets` can schedule them independently through the configured execution backend.

In practice, this is why reaction-level work, aggregation-level branches, and optional downstream modules can often run in parallel. The exact amount of parallelism depends on the active target selection, available workers, file-system throughput, and the controller setup described in [Distributed computing](distributed_computing.qmd).

```{.r filename="R"}
targets::tar_make()
```

The command above asks `targets` to build every outdated target. `targets` then follows the dependency graph, skips up-to-date work, and dispatches independent branches according to the configured controller.
